title: A published galaxy relation replayed across a whole catalogue (SPARC, 175 galaxies)
label: post-hoc

run.id: SCI-R1 run 4 (final; frozen results identical to run 3)

rows.claim: A (decisive): the fitted acceleration scale within 0.10 of the published 1.20 (1e-10 m s^-2)
rows.note: not blind: the published values were known when the tolerances were set; fitted 1.0989, off by 0.1012; five reasonable weightings span 0.97 to 1.16

rows.claim: S-v (decisive): vertical rms scatter within 0.02 dex of the published 0.13
S-o: orthogonal rms scatter within 0.02 dex of the published 0.13

bar.text: headline: PASS only if A and S-v both PASS

rows.claim: C3: published V_flat replays from the rows, or both agree no flat part exists (all galaxies)
rows.note: a per-galaxy verdict rule, not an aggregate bar

rows.claim: C1: flat beyond R_flat, among galaxies decided (all galaxies)
C2: baryonic excess at least 2 errV at every outer row, among galaxies decided (all galaxies)
C1, science sample, among galaxies decided

misses.description: SPARC Table1 layout defect re-confirmed: the declared byte read fails on all 175 rows; read by whitespace

scipy.odr per-point weights are broken in this install (scipy 1.14.1): any per-point sy returns the start value with info 21, so run 1 measured nothing; replaced by a direct solver behind a validation gate (Amendment 1, with the brute-force value disclosed)
the islands solver bound was too narrow in run 2 (random-island fits touched b = 3); widened in Amendment 2, primary fit unchanged to 1e-8
the frozen islands control removed the shared 1/R along with the galaxy coupling; a shared-radius variant was added post hoc (Amendment 3)
sample rows do not reproduce exactly: 3168 before the precision cut against the paper's 3149, and 2700 after it against 2693; the 153 galaxies match; unexplained
the acceleration scale replay is weighting-sensitive at the 10% level and the letter does not state its fit weights, so a byte-exact replay of the parameter is not possible from the paper alone
